[1;90mSTANDING HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [1;97m井（ㄐㄧㄥˇ）

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [1;97m井（jǐng）

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [1;97mChing / The Well

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [1;97mXLVIII. The Žing Hexagram


[1;90mHEXAGRAM:
[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m井：改邑不改井，无喪无得，往來井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m木上有水，井；君子以勞民勸相。

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m井：改邑不改井，无丧无得，往来井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m木上有水，井；君子以劳民劝相。

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mTHE WELL. The town may be changed,
  But the well cannot be changed.
  It neither decreases nor increases.
  They come and go and draw from the well.
  If one gets down almost to the water
  And the rope does not go all the way,
  Or the jug breaks, it brings misfortune.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mWater over wood: the image of THE WELL.
  Thus the superior man encourages the people at their work,
  And exhorts them to help one another.

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m(Looking at) Žing, (we think of) how (the site of) a town may be changed, while (the fashion of) its wells undergoes no change. (The water of a well) never disappears and never receives (any great) increase, and those who come and those who go can draw and enjoy the benefit. If (the drawing) have nearly been accomplished, but, before the rope has quite reached the water, the bucket is broken, this is evil.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mXLVIII. (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for water form Žing. The superior man, in accordance with this, comforts the people, and. stimulates them to mutual helpfulness.

[1;90mLINES:

[0m(Multiple moving lines)

[1;97mNo available reference scripture or exegesis for multiple moving lines.

[1;90mEMERGING HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [1;97m既濟（ㄐㄧˋ ㄐㄧˋ）

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [1;97m既济（jì jì）

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [1;97mChi Chi / After Completion

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [1;97mLXIII. The Kî Žî Hexagram


[1;90mHEXAGRAM:
[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m既濟：亨，小利貞，初吉終亂。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m水在火上，既濟；君子以思患而預防之。

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m既济：亨，小利贞，初吉终乱。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m水在火上，既济；君子以思患而预防之。

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mAFTER COMPLETION. Success in small matters.
  Perseverance furthers.
  At the beginning good fortune,
  At the end disorder.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mWater over fire: the image of the condition
  In AFTER COMPLETION.
  Thus the superior man
  Takes thought of misfortune
  And arms himself against it in advance.

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mKî Žî intimates progress and success in small matters. There will be advantage in being firm and correct. There has been good fortune in the beginning; there may be disorder in the end.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mLXIII. (The trigram representing) fire and that for water above it form Kî Žî. The superiorman, in accordance with this, thinks of evil (that may come), and beforehand guards against it.
